passage: At fifteen, Jatin spent the holidays with two grandmothers. His Nani Leela hummed while she cut vegetables, laughed at her own mistakes and told him stories about the neighbours she still visited. His Dadi Rekha sat by the window and listed who had wronged her, who had not called and what she would never forgive. Jatin watched her fold and refold the same handkerchief. On the train home, he wondered which of them he would turn out to be, and did not know how to ask. At twenty, Jatin was in his last year of college and had accepted a safe job at a bank without ever weighing another option. One evening, imagining himself at sixty, he saw the same desk, a lot of things unsaid to his father, and the drawing he had put away in a cupboard. His stomach turned. That weekend he sat down at the table with his father and told him honestly that he did not want to spend his life in a bank, and that he was afraid of disappointing him. His father was quiet for a long time, then reached for the tea.

qa.q: Who hummed while she cut vegetables?
qa.a: His Nani Leela hummed while she cut vegetables.

qa.q: How does the question Jatin forms about his grandmothers at fifteen return in a new form at twenty?
qa.a: At fifteen he watched a content grandmother beside a bitter one and wondered which he would become, and at twenty he pictured himself at sixty at a desk with words left unsaid and a drawing in a cupboard. The fear of a wasted life led him to speak honestly to his father while there was time.

qa.q: What was Jatin feeling when he pictured himself at sixty in the same bank job?
qa.a: He felt afraid and regretful, as his turning stomach shows, of a life he had never questioned.

qa.q: What could Jatin do after talking with his father to act more honestly about his drawing?
qa.a: He could set aside regular time to draw, look into courses or projects that use it, and keep talking with his father about his choices.

grounding: The same person foresees old age at two ages: contrasting a content and a bitter grandparent at fifteen, and imagining a wasted life of regrets at twenty that pushes him toward honesty.
